Hospitality is the supreme sacred ford; the guest is said to be the sacred ford. Celibacy is the supreme sacred ford; the three sacrificial fires are said to be the sacred ford.
Having understood the root of dharma, let the mind be fixed upon it.
"Go to the sacred fords (*tīrtha*), O son of Kuntī; through righteousness, dharma increases.
They say that there are two kinds of sacred fords: the stationary and the moving. Of these, the moving is superior, and therefore, the acquisition of knowledge [is the highest]."

O Bhārata, for a person purified even by action in this world, all sacred fords (tīrthas) reside within the heart; he is said to be the embodiment of all sacred fords. Supreme knowledge is the highest sacred ford; therefore, no other ford exists.
The ford of knowledge is the supreme ford, the eternal ford of Brahman;
but forbearance, O Pāṇḍava, is the highest ford among all fords.
This world belongs to those who possess forbearance, and the world beyond belongs to those who possess forbearance.
Whether honored or dishonored, whether revered or unrevered, whether dragged away or threatened—one who is patient is called a *tīrtha*.
Patience is self-restraint; patience is charity; patience is sacrifice; patience is austerity.
Forgiveness is non-violence; forgiveness is dharma; forgiveness is the restraint of the senses.
Forgiveness is compassion; forgiveness is sacrifice; by forgiveness this world is sustained. One who possesses forgiveness shall attain heaven; one who possesses forgiveness shall attain glory.
The patient man shall attain liberation; therefore, that [patience] is called a sacred ford (*tīrtha*). The self (*ātman*) is the river, the meritorious ford of Bhārata;
the self is the ford, the foremost of all sacred fords.
The self is indeed always considered to be the sacrifice;
heaven and liberation— everything is dependent upon the self by one who has attained purity of conduct.
He who indeed bathes daily with the water of knowledge— which is true, pure, patient, and cool—
Yudhiṣṭhira said:
"What further need has he for water?
"Lord, there is an expiation that destroys all sins and is not difficult to perform.
The Blessed One said:

O best of gods, you ought to tell this to me, your devotee; for this secret is exceedingly unfit to be heard by those of sinful deeds and unfit to be heard by the unrighteous. I shall declare this expiation to you.
Upon seeing a purifying Brāhmaṇa, with his inner self absorbed in me,
he should perform a salutation, saying: "Obeisance to the God who is the Friend of Brahman," and he should circumambulate him three times, again reciting the eight-syllabled mantra.
O best of men, being pleased by that, I shall destroy that sin.
Wherever a man carries on his head the earth dug up by a boar,
he is liberated from all sins after performing one hundred breath-restraints (*prāṇāyāma*).
Whether from a right-spiraling conch shell or even from the horn of a tawny cow,
having gone to a river flowing eastward in the vicinity of my sanctuary,
whoever bathes there even once during a solar eclipse—
Whatever sin has been accumulated by him perishes at that very moment,
O Yudhiṣṭhira, by the waters flowing from the head of a Kapilā cow,
or by one who bathes with cow urine on the day of Rohiṇī or on my own day.
Even by the waters falling from the feet of a Brahmin, sin is destroyed. But he who bows with devotion to me to Śiṃśumāra, the Lord of Creatures,
who is endowed with fourteen limbs— his sin is destroyed.

Then, O lord of men, hear of its fourteen constituent parts: Dharma is the head, Brahmā is the jaw, and the north and south are the two tails. Viṣṇu is the heart, and the two Aśvins are the two hands.
O King, Agni should be the middle; the *liṅga* should be for one year.
Mitra and Varuṇa are the two feet, and Hutāśana is the base of the tail. Behind that is Indra, and behind him is Prajāpati.
And after that, he is indeed known as Dhruva, representing fearlessness.
All these are the limbs of the Prajāpati Śiṃśumāra.
One should drink the five products of the cow (pañcagavya) after fasting on the full moon day.
All that sin previously accumulated is destroyed for him. Likewise, he who drinks the *brahmakūrca* separately each month, accompanied by its respective mantras, his sin is utterly annihilated.
O Bhārata, hear now about the sin, the *brahmakūrca* rite, and the mantra.
Having placed a vessel made of *pālāśa* wood, a lotus leaf, copper, or even gold, one should take hold of it; that is what is called the vessel.
Taking cow urine with the *gāyatrī* verse, cow dung with "gandhadvārā," milk with "āpyāyasva," curd with "dadhikrāvṇo," clarified butter with "tejo 'si śukram," and *kuśa*-water with "devasya."
Having gathered barley flour according to the prescribed rule with the mantra "āpo hi ṣṭhā," and having offered it to Brahmā as well as into the kindled fire,
one should stir it with the *praṇava* alone and churn it with the *praṇava*.
Having extracted [the water] with the *praṇava* alone, he should drink it with the *praṇava* alone;
even by great sin, he is liberated like a snake from its skin.
He who recites the verse beginning with "bhadraṃ naḥ" according to the *Ṛgveda-saṃhitā*, [attains the same].
Whether in the water or before the sun, his sin is destroyed. He who, with his mind fixed on me, constantly recites my hymn—
Yudhiṣṭhira said:
One would not be stained by evil, just as a lotus leaf is not wetted by water.
"O Lord of the Gods, what kind of Brahmins are meritorious and pure in their inner being?
The Blessed One said:
"O Acyuta, tell me which action is fruitful and which is not. "Listen, O Pāṇḍava, to all that regarding the Brāhmaṇas in due order;
I shall describe to you their actions, both those that are fruitful and those that are fruitless."
Carrying the triple staff, observing silence, wearing matted hair or shaving the head; dwelling in bark garments or deerskins, performing vows, ritual ablutions,
maintaining the sacred fire, living in the forest, Vedic study, giving gifts, and performing hospitable rites.

All these are indeed false if one’s state of being is not pure. O King, the *agnihotra* sacrifice is in vain, and the Vedas are likewise in vain; the gods are pleased by conduct alone—that is the reason for the sacred scriptures.

One who is patient, self-controlled, who has conquered anger, mastered the self, and subdued the senses—I consider him to be the foremost Brāhmaṇa; all others are traditionally known as Śūdras. [I consider] those who are devoted to the Agnihotra vow, dedicated to the study of the Vedas, and pure—[to be the foremost Brāhmaṇas].
The gods know those who are devoted to fasting and self-restrained as true Brahmins.
O King, birth is not what is honored; rather, virtues are the cause of auspiciousness. Even a Caṇḍāla who stands firm in right conduct—the gods know him as a Brahmin.
O Bhārata, purity of mind, purity of action, purity of lineage,
purity of body, and purity of speech— these are remembered as the five kinds of purity.
Among these five purities, purity of heart is distinguished as the most excellent.

By purity of heart, however, human beings go to heaven. A Brāhmaṇa who has fallen away from the Agnihotra sacrifice, who is addicted to buying and selling, and who causes the intermixture of castes, is equal to a Śūdra.

O son of Kuntī, he whose Vedic revelation has been lost, the twice-born who is a mere farmer, and he who follows improper occupations—he is indeed called a *vṛṣala*. For *vṛṣa* should be understood as dharma; he who causes its destruction is a *vṛṣala*.
The gods know that man to be a *vṛṣala*, more base even than a dog-cooker (*śvapaca*),
who praises a *śūdra* with hymns purified by the Veda;
that evil-souled man does not praise me, but rather reviles me most severely.
Just as milk in a dog’s heat becomes spoiled, so too does the Brahman [Veda] when it reaches a *vṛṣala*;
all that becomes defiled, like an oblation licked by a dog.
The limbs [of knowledge] are the four Vedas, Mīmāṃsā, and the expansion of Nyāya.
The Dharmaśāstra and the Purāṇa— these, O Bhārata, are indeed the fourteen branches of knowledge (vidyāsthāna) which I have correctly described to you;
they have arisen as pure means for the sake of purification.
Therefore, O Yudhiṣṭhira, those [objects] must not be touched by a Śūdra;
everything touched by a Śūdra is impure, without a doubt. O Bhārata, there are three things in the world that are impure and five that are unholy.
O Pāṇḍava, a dog, a Śūdra, and a dog-cooker (śvapāka) are impure things. A deity-image, a cock, a sacrificial post, a menstruating woman, and the husband of a low-caste woman—
these five are unholy and must not be touched under any circumstances.
Having touched these eight, a Brahmin should indeed enter the water with his clothes on.
Those men who despise my devotees as if they were common Śūdras—
those lowest of men— shall remain in the hells for ten million years.
A wise person should not despise even a Caṇḍāla who is my devotee;
for by despising him, men surely fall into the Raurava hell.
O King, my love for those who are devoted to my devotees is even greater.

Therefore, those who are devoted to my devotees are especially worthy of worship. Know that even for worms, birds, and beasts whose minds are surrendered to me, their destination is surely upward; how much more so for wise men?
Whether it be a leaf, or even a flower, a fruit, or even water—
if a Śūdra gives these to me, I bear them upon my head; indeed, a Śūdra who generally honors Brāhmaṇas with devotion is dear to me.
O Bhārata, I accept their worship in that very form;
abiding in the hearts of all beings, those brahmins worship me according to the path declared in the Vedas, and they attain union with me.
My manifestation has been brought about solely for the welfare of my devotees.
O Yudhiṣṭhira, some particular form of this manifestation is worthy of worship. Whoever worships any one of these forms with devotion to me—
I shall be fully satisfied by that alone, there is no doubt;
whether by means of clay, precious gems, copper, silver,
or even gold, one should fashion an image and perform worship.
One should know that the merit of these [acts] increases tenfold for each subsequent one. A king desiring victory, the best of the twice-born desiring knowledge,
a Vaiśya desiring wealth, or a Śūdra fond of the fruits of merit should worship them.
"Even all women shall obtain all their desires.
Yudhiṣṭhira said:
"But for what kind of Śūdras do you not accept worship?"
The Blessed One said:
"O Lord of the Gods, tell me why you are distressed? Why is it that this worship has been touched by one who is neither observing vows nor devoted, and even by a Śūdra?"

I avoid that [speech] with great effort, as if it were uttered by an outcaste. Indeed, O Yudhiṣṭhira, both I and Śaṅkara, as well as cows, Brahmins, and the Aśvattha tree, are my forms; this is the truth.

My devotee should never, at any time, hold these three in contempt; for when they are held in contempt, they burn the family unto the seventh generation. The *aśvattha* tree, the Brahmins, and the cows—these, being composed of me, deliver one from saṃsāra.
Yudhiṣṭhira said:
Therefore, O Pāṇḍava, worship these three with great effort. How could one attain the state of a Śūdra while still possessing a Brāhmaṇa body?
The Blessed One said:
"O Lord, you ought to tell me how even the Brahman might perish.
If a Brahmin should perform the ritual bath at a well for twelve years..."
With that very body, he undoubtedly attains the state of a Śūdra. But that Brāhmaṇa who lives for twelve years solely by depending upon a king—
even if he has mastered the Vedas— shall fall into the state of a Śūdra.

If a Brahmin should dwell in the city of Pattana for twelve years, he shall live in the state of a Śūdra; there is no need for deliberation on this point. Furthermore, if a twice-born man intentionally begets a son upon a Śūdra woman...
The Brahman residing within his body perishes instantly.
That man who, out of delusion, tastes the face of a woman while intoxicated by liquor—
the Brahman residing within his body perishes instantly.
O King, if a Brahmin should consume the *soma* creeper in vain,
without [proper ritual], the *brahman* residing within his body perishes instantly. Furthermore, O King, that Brahmin who engages in sexual intercourse with it upon his tongue [is likewise lost].

The Brahman residing within his body perishes instantly. Having attained this Brahminhood, which is so difficult to obtain, those who destroy it through such evil paths— of them I grieve, O Yudhiṣṭhira.
Therefore, with every effort, O Yudhiṣṭhira who is dear to me,
a twice-born man should not perform such an act that causes the loss of his caste.
Yudhiṣṭhira said:
When a Brahmin who has gone to another land is joined with the law of time,
the Blessed One said:
"When the destruction of the body has occurred, how can there be a conceptualization of a 'preta'?"

Listen now to the ritual for one who has maintained the sacred fires and passed away in such a state. An image should be fashioned from the stalks of *pālāśa* leaves, as prescribed by the ritual manuals.
O lord of men, they say that his bones number three hundred and sixty.
One should perform their ritual dismemberment according to the determination of the scriptures:
fifty on the head, ten on the neck,
one hundred on the two arms, and again ten on the fingers.
One should inflict thirty [strokes] on the chest and twenty on the abdomen;
twelve and a half on the testicles and likewise eight and a half on the penis;
one hundred on the thighs and sixty and a half on the knees and shanks.
One should give ten [coins] at the feet; this is the expiation for the deceased.
Yudhiṣṭhira said:
[Tell me of] a distinguished sacred ford that grants grace to all who are incapable.
The Blessed One said:
"For the sake of delivering devotees, you ought indeed to speak according to the Dharma;
for the chanters of the Sāman hymns sing that truth is the most excellent of all sacred fords."
Speaking the truth is a sacred ford; non-violence is said to be a sacred ford. Asceticism is a sacred ford, compassion is a sacred ford, and good conduct is a sacred ford, O Yudhiṣṭhira.
Contentment with little is a sacred ford, and a wife devoted to her husband is a sacred ford.

A contented Brahmin is a sacred ford (*tīrtha*); knowledge is also called a sacred ford. My devotee is always a sacred ford, especially that of Śaṅkara. Ascetics are indeed sacred fords; the wise are said to be sacred fords.

The man who provides refuge is a sacred ford; the giver of food is said to be a sacred ford. In these three worlds, I am free from anxiety and fear nothing whatsoever—neither by day nor by night do I have any agitation regarding the transgression of a Śūdra.
"O King, I have no fear of gods, daityas, or even rākṣasas;
but, O observer of noble vows, I do have fear of the Veda falling from the mouth of a Śūdra.
Therefore, a Śūdra should not utter even my name accompanied by the *praṇava*."

The knowers of Brahman know the *praṇava* to be indeed the supreme Brahman, eternal. For the *śūdras*, the duty is service to the twice-born with devotion toward me; by that, they go to heaven, for they are constantly meditating upon me.
Through service to the twice-born, a Śūdra attains the highest good. There is no other means of atonement for a Śūdra than service to the twice-born.
Passion, hatred, delusion, harshness, and cruelty—[these are the obstacles].
Deceit, long-standing enmity, excessive pride, lack of uprightness,
falsehood, slander, maliciousness, and extreme greed;
violence, theft, lying, deception, and the state of being prone to anger and avarice.
Lack of intelligence, atheism, fear, and indolence;
impurity, ingratitude, hypocrisy, and arrogance;
as well as deceit and ignorance—these enter a Śūdra at birth.
Seeing that the Śūdra was overwhelmed by qualities of darkness (tamas), the Grandfather (Pitāmaha) prescribed service to the twice-born as the duty for Śūdras;
through devotion to the twice-born, the dark dispositions of the Śūdra perish.
"Whoever offers Me with devotion a leaf, a flower, a fruit, or water— that offering made with devotion, even from a Śūdra, I accept upon my head—
even if he be an outcaste or anyone else who is burdened with every kind of sin."

If one should constantly meditate upon me, they shall be liberated from all sins. Those Brahmins who are endowed with learning and humility and have mastered the Vedas, yet do not practice devotion toward me, are indeed like outcasts.
Whatever is given in vain, whatever is muttered in vain, whatever is performed in vain, and whatever is offered in sacrifice in vain—
even hospitality rendered in vain— belongs to that twice-born who is not devoted to me.
Whatever has been done, whatever has been offered in sacrifice, whatever has been desired, and whatever has been given [is likewise fruitless].
All that is offered without devotion is consumed by the Rākṣasas alone.
O Pāṇḍava, when my devotee acts with equanimity toward all beings— whether stationary or moving— and likewise toward friends and enemies, [then his offerings are truly made].
O King, compassion, non-violence, mercy, truthfulness, uprightness,
and freedom from malice toward all beings— this is the vow of those devoted to me. Even he who, endowed with faith, merely utters "Namaḥ" (Salutation) to me is my devotee.
O Pāṇḍava, even for an outcaste, his world shall become inexhaustible;
how much more so for those priests who worship me according to the prescribed rites,
who are my devotees, whose lives are dedicated to me, and who always speak of me?
Even a man who performs austerities for many thousands of years does not attain that state which is attained by my devotees;
therefore, O Indra among kings, meditate upon me alone constantly and without weariness.
"From that you shall attain perfection; you shall behold the supreme state.
Those who speak meaninglessly claim, 'Śūdras are Bhāgavatas. Śūdras are not devotees of the Blessed One; it is the Brahmins who are remembered as Bhāgavatas."
One who knows the reality of the twelve syllables, who understands the division of the fourfold manifestation (caturvyūha),
who is faultless, and who knows the five periods of time— he indeed is remembered as a Bhāgavata.
By means of the Ṛgveda alone the Hotṛ priest [worships] me, and by means of the Yajurveda the Adhvaryu likewise.
The Udgātṛ priest praises me with the meritorious Sāmaveda;
and the twice-born Atharvaṇas always praise me with the Atharvaśiras. Those who constantly praise me in this way are also remembered as Bhāgavatas.
Sacrifices are always dependent upon the Vedas, and the deities are dependent upon the sacrifices;
the deities are dependent upon the Brahmins; therefore, the Brahmins are indeed the deities. Without depending on support, there is no rising up; one should rely upon the primary support.
The gods have taken refuge in Rudra; Rudra has taken refuge in the Brāhmaṇa;
O King, Brahmā has taken refuge in me, but I have not taken refuge in anyone. Indeed, there is no one who is my refuge; rather, I am the refuge of all.
Thus has this supreme secret been proclaimed by me; O King, you who are fond of dharma, always conduct yourself in this manner. This sacred narrative is meritorious and equal to the Veda.
O Pāṇḍava, for one who recites my Dharma day after day,
his righteousness increases and his intellect becomes clear;
indeed, his evil is destroyed and his welfare flourishes.
This merit is pure, supreme, and the destroyer of sins;
it should be heard with faith, especially by those learned in the Vedas (*śrotriya*).
Whoever, being self-restrained, recites this with devotion or listens to it, [attains the highest reward].
He shall attain union with me; there is no need for deliberation on this point.
And he who, being my devotee and devoted to me, causes this to be heard at a *śrāddha* ceremony—Vaiśampāyana said:
His ancestors remain satisfied until the dissolution of all beings,
having heard the Bhāgavata duties directly from Viṣṇu, the Teacher of the World,
and having become joyful in mind, reflecting upon those wonderful stories.
The ṛṣis and the Pāṇḍavas likewise bowed down to that Janārdana. Dharmaputra honored Govinda again and again;
so too did the gods, the brahmarṣis, the siddhas, the gandharvas, and the apsarases.
The *bhūtas*, *yakṣas*, and *grahas*, as well as the *guhyakas* and *bhujaṅgas*;
the high-souled *vālakhilyas*, the *yogins* who perceive reality;
and likewise the *bhāgavatas* who practice worship at the five times of day.
Filled with curiosity, O Blessed One, they have come here with devotion;
having heard this supreme and most meritorious teaching of the Vaiṣṇava dharma,
they have become purified and freed from sin at that very moment.
Having bowed their heads to Viṣṇu and rejoiced in that discourse,
they said, "We shall all behold the Teacher of the World in Dvārakā," and with joyful hearts, they departed along with the hosts of gods.
O King, all the hosts of ṛṣis went each to his own abode. When they had all departed, O King, Keśava, the slayer of Keśin, then remembered Dāruka, who was together with Sātyaki.
The charioteer stood nearby and said, "Go,
O Lord. Then the Pāṇḍavas, their faces dejected,
placed their joined palms upon their heads and looked at the Supreme Person with eyes overflowing with tears.
Constantly drinking [the nectar] of Kṛṣṇa, they did not speak at all, being then overcome by extreme distress.
The blessed Lord Kṛṣṇa, having addressed Pṛthā like one in pain,
as well as Dhṛtarāṣṭra, Gāndhārī, Vidura, and Draupadī, likewise—
Having touched Kṛṣṇadvaipāyana Vyāsa, the other sages, and his ministers, and having touched Subhadrā along with her son and Uttarā with his hand,
he departed from that palace and ascended his great chariot.
Yoked with the horses Sainya, Sugrīva, Meghapuṣpa, and Balāhaka, and with the wise king of birds as its banner,
King Yudhiṣṭhira ascended it out of affection.
Then the lord of the Kurus quickly dismissed Dāruka, the best of charioteers, and took up the reins himself;
and Arjuna also ascended, taking up the beautiful yak-tail fan.
He whirled a large golden-handled [staff] clockwise above his head,
and a parasol with a hundred ribs, adorned with divine garlands,
and one with a handle of lapis lazuli gems, decorated with refined gold.
The formidable Bhīma swiftly held the umbrella of the wielder of the Śārṅga bow;
and Bhīmasena, Arjuna, and the two sons of Yama, the destroyers of enemies,
followed behind Kṛṣṇa, filled with joy, lest there be any noise.

When three *yojanas* had passed, Kṛṣṇa embraced the Pāṇḍavas; having bid farewell to all of them as they bowed down, he departed for Dvārakā. Likewise, from that time forward, the Pāṇḍavas continued to bow down to Govinda.
Devoted to righteousness, the Pāṇḍavas gave gifts such as those of Kapilā cows; repeatedly recollecting the words of Madhusūdana, they honored them in their minds, held within their hearts.

But the righteous-souled Yudhiṣṭhira, having taken Janārdana to heart, became devoted to him, focused on him, intent on sacrificing for him, and dedicated to him. Thus was this ancient account, the Vaiṣṇava ordinance of dharma.
O King, I have told you this sacred teaching that destroys all sin. Listen to it, O Great King, descendant of Kuru, for it was proclaimed by Viṣṇu himself;
by this alone, and no other way, shall you go to that supreme abode of Viṣṇu.
